questions.q: In ComfyUI, what does the denoise value of an img2img KSampler change?
options: It adds that fraction of noise to the encoded image
It picks where on a longer noise schedule the sampler starts, so the first noise level depends on denoise
It sets how many steps run
It blends the output with the input image afterwards
questions.answer: It picks where on a longer noise schedule the sampler starts, so the first noise level depends on denoise
questions.why: KSampler.set_steps builds a schedule of int(steps / denoise) steps and keeps the last steps + 1 values. The number of steps run stays 20 in the lab, and the first sigma is 0.552, 1.548 or 4.904 for denoise 0.2, 0.5 or 0.8.

questions.q: In the lab, denoise 0.5 starts at sigma 1.548. How much of the clean latent's signal does the starting latent keep, for unit-variance latents?
options: 0.5, because denoise is 0.5
About 0.54, which is 1 / √(1 + 1.548²)
About 0.2
questions.why: The start is L + σ n, so its correlation with L is 1 / √(1 + σ²). The lab measures 0.542 against the formula's 0.543.

questions.q: A ControlNet has start_percent 0 and end_percent 0.5 on an SD 1.x model. What window does that set?
options: The first half of the steps, whatever the scheduler
The steps where the noise level is at or above the level at timestep 499.5, which is 10 of 20 steps on the normal scheduler and 9 on Karras
Half of the strength
The steps after the noise level drops below 1
questions.answer: The steps where the noise level is at or above the level at timestep 499.5, which is 10 of 20 steps on the normal scheduler and 9 on Karras
questions.why: pre_run_control maps the percents through percent_to_sigma, which reads the noise level at timestep (1 − percent) · 999. The lab prints a stop level of 1.616 and 10 and 9 steps.

questions.q: Why can a ControlNet with zero-initialised output convolutions still learn, even though its output starts at zero?
options: The gradient of the zero convolution's own weights is not zero, and once they move the trainable copy and the input convolution get gradients
Zero convolutions are replaced by random ones after the first step
The locked model supplies the gradient
Zero convolutions are never trained
questions.answer: The gradient of the zero convolution's own weights is not zero, and once they move the trainable copy and the input convolution get gradients
questions.why: The weight gradient depends on the convolution's input, not on its weights. The gradient to the copy passes through the zero weights, so it is 0.0000 at step 0 and 0.0019 after one step in the lab.

questions.q: Is IP-Adapter part of ComfyUI core v0.43.0?
options: Yes, as the IPAdapterApply node
No: a search of the core sources finds no mention of it, so it comes from custom nodes. Core has StyleModelApply and unCLIPConditioning for image prompts
Yes, but only for SDXL
No, and ComfyUI has no way to use an image as a prompt
questions.answer: No: a search of the core sources finds no mention of it, so it comes from custom nodes. Core has StyleModelApply and unCLIPConditioning for image prompts
questions.why: A case-insensitive search of comfy/, comfy_extras/, comfy_api/ and nodes.py finds nothing. StyleModelApply and unCLIPConditioning are in nodes.py.

questions.q: In the lab's attention test, what happens when appended image tokens are multiplied by a strength of 0, as StyleModelApply does in multiply mode?
options: The result equals a layer with no image, difference 0.0
The tokens remain in the attention and change the result, by 0.34 in the lab
The layer raises an error
The result equals the decoupled form with lambda 1
questions.answer: The tokens remain in the attention and change the result, by 0.34 in the lab
questions.why: A zero token still takes attention weight, so it dilutes the text tokens. Decoupled cross-attention with lambda 0 matches the no-image layer exactly, and attn_bias mode, which adds log(0) = -inf, does too (2.4e-07).
